texts.preamble: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector vs Pramod Kumar Jain on 19 September, 2016
texts.facts: Accused JUDGMENT: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (PFA Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules. The accused Pramod Kumar Jain is stated to be the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s. Shahi Bhog, from where the food article, that is, 'Khoya Burfi' was lifted for sampling. 2. As per the complaint, on 10.11.2004, the food officials consisting of Food Inspector (FI) Ranjeet Singh and Field Assistant (FA) Mittra Pal under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Sh. C. P. Sharma reached along with their staff at the premises of M/s. Shahi Bhog, at F-3/5, Krishna Nagar, Delhi-51, where the accused was found conducting the business of various food articles, which were lying stored/exposed for sale for human consumption. The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of Khoya Burfi from the vendor, to which he had agreed. The sample was then lifted as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules. Each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed and necessary documents were prepared at the spot, including the notice as per Form-VI, panchnama, etc. The price of sample was paid to the vendor. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample was sent to the Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and the other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. Vide report dated Delhi Administration / Food Inspector vs Pramod Kumar Jain on 19 September, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80700135/ 1 02.12.2004, the PA found the sample to be adulterated on the ground that it contained added vegetable oil which was not declared as an ingredient. Upon receipt of report, the SDM/LHA ordered investigation which was carried out by FI. After completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 02.03.2005 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a) and (b) of PFA Act as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act. 3. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 02.03.2005. The accused appeared and filed an application under section 13(2) of PFA Act on 10.04.2007 thereby exercising his right to get the second counterpart of the sample analysed from Central Food Laboratory (CFL). However, vide order dated 13.04.2007, the said application was dismissed being not maintainable as the delay could not be condoned. Thereafter, notice of accusation under section 251 CrPC was framed against him on 14.07.2008 for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1)(a) PFA Act, being violation of section 2(ia)(a) and (b) of PFA Act, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 4. At the trial, prosecution examined three witnesses in support of its case. PW-1 was the LHA/SDM, PW-2 was the FI and PW-3 was the FA who were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings. All these witnesses deposed about the proceedings conducted by them on 10.11.2004 and narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of 1500 gms of Khoya Burfi, cutting the same into smallest possible pieces using a clean and dry knife, mixing/homogenizing it using a clean and dry spoon, dividing it in three parts and putting in clean and dry bottles, adding formalin (40 drops each) as preservative, fastening, sealing, marking the sample bottles, and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A and issuance of cash memo Ex. PW-1/A1, Notice in Form-VI Ex. PW-1/B and Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C. One sample was deposited with PA vide PA Receipt Ex. PW-1/E and two counterparts with LHA vide receipt Ex. PW-1/D. PA report Ex. PW-1/F was received upon which investigation was carried out by PW-2. Letter Ex. PW-2/A was written to accused which was not replied and letter Ex. PW-2/B was written to STO which was replied. After completion of investigation, sanction Ex. PW-1/G was taken from the Director PFA and the complaint Ex. PW-1/H was filed in the court. A copy of PA report with intimation letter Ex. PW-1/I was sent to the accused through registered post vide receipt Ex. PW-1/J. These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel wherein they denied that the sampling method was not proper or that the spoon / bottles used in the proceedings were not clean and dry. 5. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC was recorded on 04.05.2012 wherein he denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Though he admitted the proceedings dated 10.11.2004, yet he claimed that no efforts were made to join public witnesses and that the bottles used were not clean and dry. He took stand that he had added badam and pista in the article which contains vegetable oil. He stated that vanaspati was not added as an ingredient but his worker had pasted some vegetable oil in the tray to avoid sticking of burfi with the tray. He chose to lead evidence in defence. Delhi Administration / Food Inspector vs Pramod Kumar Jain on 19 September, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80700135/ 2 6. The accused summoned record of a letter no. P-150 16/3/83- PH(F&N) PFA dated 17.10.1984, and proved it though DW-1. 7. The accused also examined Sh. S. N. Mahendru, a food chemical expert as DW-1 (sic: DW-1A). He deposed that glycerine and vegetable oil are allowed as Good Manufacturing Practices so that the material does not stick to the container. He further stated that almond seeds and pista have oil content in them. During cross-examination, he stated that almond oil, pista oil and other vegetable oils have different chemical compositions which can be identified and that the analyst is required to identify which other oil is present in the article.
texts.arguments: 8. It is in these circumstances, Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to establish its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt, on the ground that the accused has not been able to rebut the findings in the PA report dated 02.12.2004. It is submitted that all the witnesses have supported its case and no major contradiction can be seen in their testimony. 9. On the other hand, Ld. Defence Counsel has submitted that the sample proceedings were not conducted properly and that there are various contradictions and missing links in the testimony of witnesses. Ld. Counsel has contended that the sample of burfi contained almonds and pista which were declared as ingredients and they have their own inherent oil. It is submitted that vegetable oil is permitted to be used as a lubricant and that the accused had used oil on the tray so that the food article does not stick to the tray. It is then argued that as per Rule 43(5) of PFA Rules, a seller of sweets is not required to declare the ingredients and thus, there is no violation of rules. It is also argued that the complaint was filed after three months of lifting the sample which caused prejudice to the accused as he could not exercise his right under section 13(2) PFA Act on time. 12. Under section 2(ia)(a) of PFA Act, the prosecution has to establish that the purchaser had demanded a food article of a specific nature, substance or quality and the article sold was, to his prejudice, either not of the nature, substance or quality demanded, or was not of the nature, substance or quality which it purported or represented to be. Ld. Defence Counsel while arguing the matter contended that the prosecution has not ruled out various possibilities of using contaminated utensils / implements, possibility of improper sampling, possibility of the vegetable oil being added subsequently, possibility of the vegetable oil coming into the food product as GMP through the tray on which it was kept, possibility of the PA having added the BR value of pista and almond oil in giving his opinion etc. 38.
